transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Northfield CTO), Sara Liu (Northfield ML Eng), Evan Park (Northfield Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial): agreed to run initial bench with 1k queries, Redwood to deliver golden prompts and rubric, Northfield to provide anonymized queries and edge cases. Focus on hallucination gating and strict format checks for JSON outputs.

[00:00] Alex Chen: okay uh hey everyone thanks for carving time, this is Alex from Redwood, joining me is Priya, our solutions eng. today we're here to scope the POC quality plan and make sure success criteria and the workload sizing are clear.
[00:18] Michael Torres: thanks Alex, yeah we got a lot riding on this one — primary goal is automated extraction for invoices and receipts so format correctness is huge, hallucinations are a show-stopper.
[00:32] Priya Raman: totally, so quick framing: we usually define three buckets of evals — golden prompts for correctness on canonical cases, regression tests for typical and edge-case failures, and hallucination/format gating for safety and downstream ingestion.
[00:50] Sara Liu: quick question, when you say golden prompts do you mean a single prompt template or a set per use-case?
[00:58] Priya Raman: set per use-case; for invoice extraction we'd have a canonical set for invoice layouts, one for receipts, and a set of malformed inputs to test robustness. we'll provide both the prompts and expected structured outputs.
[01:15] Evan Park: also timeline — we need something that shows impact before end of Q2, so ideally the first benchmark run in two weeks?
[01:25] Alex Chen: yes we're targeting a 2026-05-28 bench window. Redwood will provision a dedicated run slot for you; if needed we can fall back to hosted with pinned model versions for comparability.
[01:39] Michael Torres: pinned model versions is important, our compliance folks will want deterministic baselines for acceptance.
[01:46] Priya Raman: agreed. success criteria proposal: 1) format pass rate >= 98% on golden set, 2) regression pass rate >= 95% on typical workload, 3) hallucination rate < 1% on edge-case set, and 4) latency p95 under 350ms for single-row extraction in Dedicated config. Thoughts?
[02:10] Sara Liu: 98% is ambitious, but acceptable if we know what counts as a pass — is whitespace/ordering considered a fail?
[02:19] Priya Raman: good point — we'll define tolerance rules. minor whitespace or ordering differences that don't affect downstream JSON parsing will be allowed; structural mismatches or missing required fields will count as fails. we'll codify this in the rubric.
[02:35] Alex Chen: also cost ballpark: for the bench runs we'll estimate per-token cost but for Northfield's volume we can suggest quantized variants and batching options to bring unit cost down.
[02:48] Michael Torres: our monthly volume estimate is roughly 18M extractions, peak concurrency for ingestion is about ~120 qps. That should feed into workload sizing.
[02:58] Priya Raman: okay for workload sizing we typically recommend three tiers in the POC: 1) micro — 1k queries for quality, 2) sim load — 50k short-run for throughput observing p95/p99 latency, 3) long-run — 500k to validate caching and rolling sequences. For your 18M month projection sim load helps us model autoscaling and cost.
[03:22] Evan Park: can the sim load be synthetic or does it need to be all real samples?
[03:27] Priya Raman: a mix is fine — representative real samples to preserve distribution, plus synthetic edge-cases to stress format parsing.
[03:33] Speaker 1: um excuse me, are we capturing both correctness and scoring?
[03:37] Alex Chen: yes scoring approach: for structured extraction we'll do field-level exact match, field-level fuzzy match (e.g., address normalization), and an overall document pass/fail. We'll compute precision/recall for optional fields. We'll also attach a confidence binning so we can recommend thresholds to auto-accept versus human review.
[03:58] Michael Torres: confidence binning would be great. for legal reasons we need audit logs; are those included in the POC?
[04:05] Priya Raman: yes, Redwood can enable trace-level logs for each request including model version, runtime config, and token counts. we can provide them as part of the bench artifact bundle. note: logs will be scrubbed for PII if you need.
[04:20] Sara Liu: about hallucination checks — how do you define hallucination for structured extraction? sometimes model invents an invoice number that isn't there.
[04:29] Priya Raman: we define hallucination as any non-ground-truth value inserted into required fields or paraphrased values that change semantics. for invoice numbers we compare tokens to OCR layer or absence/presence — we flag mismatch as hallucination. there will be a severity score; high-severity hallucinations block acceptance.
[04:49] Michael Torres: and format checks — we require strict JSON schema adherence for ingestion, so the rubric needs machine-checkable rules.
[04:57] Alex Chen: we'll deliver a JSON Schema and a small validator harness; the rubric will include sample failing cases and expected errors.
[05:06] Evan Park: can we also test reranking / fallback behavior? e.g., when primary model fails format, call a lightweight model to try format-only extraction?
[05:15] Priya Raman: yes that's part of the smart routing discussion — for POC we can simulate fallbacks; we'll record end-to-end latency and success after fallback. note that fallback costs extra but improves reliability.
[05:28] Michael Torres: compliance note: our security reviewer wants SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and a SOC2 report. Alex, can you send that?
[05:36] Alex Chen: yes I'll email Redwood's compliance pack — SSO guides, KMS patterns, SOC2 attestations. I'll add links in the follow-up.
[05:44] Speaker 2 (maybe automated): [unintelligible]...
[05:48] Priya Raman: back to scoring — we'll propose a weighted scoring formula: 50% golden set accuracy, 20% regression pass-rate, 15% hallucination severity-adjusted metric, 15% latency cost-efficiency score. the weightings are negotiable.
[06:05] Sara Liu: can you show an example of the golden prompts and expected outputs? even a couple so we can validate format?
[06:11] Priya Raman: sure, I'll drop two examples in the shared drive: one invoice canonical prompt expecting {invoice_number, date, total_amount, vendor.name} and another receipt prompt. they will include canonical wording and model temperature/stop sequences.
[06:29] Alex Chen: note on transcription quality: some product names get misheard — we sometimes see 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V cash' — ignore odd rendering in auto docs.
[06:41] Michael Torres: haha noted.
[06:43] [08:02] (discussion continues; technical deep-dive between Priya and Sara)
[08:02] Priya Raman: for regressions we'll set up unit tests that re-run failing prompt+input pairs on new model versions; each failing case will be triaged and labeled as 'behavior change' vs 'regression error'.
[08:20] Sara Liu: what's the target false positive rate for hallucination alarms?
[08:24] Priya Raman: aim is <1% on the edge-case set; for alerting we can tune thresholds to trade recall vs precision — you're likely to want higher precision to avoid noise.
[08:35] Evan Park: for timeline, can we get an initial pass within five business days after dataset handoff?
[08:40] Alex Chen: yes with the 1k canonical set we'll run the golden prompt bench within 3 business days; the larger sim loads take longer.
[08:50] Michael Torres: anything around data residency? we need EU-only processing for some customers — how does Redwood handle region pinning?
[08:58] Priya Raman: Redwood supports region pinning in Hosted and Dedicated; for Private deployments we can run in your VPC if needed. we'll include region flags in the bench config.
[09:09] Sara Liu: one more technical: how are you handling tokenization differences impacting exact-match scoring? sometimes punctuation or unicode differences cause false negatives.
[09:18] Priya Raman: our scoring supports normalization rules — unicode normalization, punctuation stripping for certain fields, and canonical number parsing. we'll include normalization steps in the rubric and allow you to opt-in/out per-field.
[09:34] [12:10] (short cross-talk)
[12:10] Alex Chen: recap and next steps quick: Redwood to upload golden prompts + rubric (Priya) by Friday; Northfield to share 1k anonymized queries and 100 labeled edge cases (Sara) by Tuesday; schedule bench run for 2026-05-28 (Alex) — we'll send calendar hold. security docs out tomorrow.
[12:36] Michael Torres: good recap. one ask: can we get example evaluation dashboards so stakeholders can see pass/fail and per-field breakdown?
[12:45] Alex Chen: yes we'll attach the dashboard template and a sample run export.
[12:51] Evan Park: ok thanks everyone, excited to see initial results.
[12:55] Priya Raman: thanks, we'll follow up with links and the spreadsheet.
[13:00] (meeting ends)

Post-meeting note (auto): Shared drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/northfield-poc (redwood will fill with golden_prompts.csv, rubric.md, bench-config.yaml). Benchmark artifact: bench-report-20260528-placeholder (to be created after run).
